fig4.claim: For each same-study pair, the sign of the predicted heterogeneous-barrier difference (test minus reference) agrees with the observed ordering of the two surfaces when its 90 % interval excludes zero on the observed side.
fig4.caption_key: (a) One row per usable case (identifiers RC01 to RC12, defined in the caption with their surfaces and study). Marker: median of the predicted difference Delta = DG*_het(test) - DG*_het(reference) over the Monte Carlo draws, in units of k_B T; bar: its 5 % to 95 % interval. Marker shape and colour give the verdict of the pass criterion: filled circle, correct; filled square, incorrect; open diamond, inconclusive (the interval contains zero, which counts as not correct). Vertical line: Delta = 0. Horizontal axis linear within +-1 k_B T and logarithmic beyond. (b) Observed ordering of the same case: right-pointing triangle, test surface has the higher barrier; left-pointing, the lower. The caption states N, the number correct, k and the chance probability from the record's summary, and each case's boundary mass.

fig5.claim: At equilibrium the template acts on the barrier only through the wetting angle: at a given bulk saturation ratio the barrier on the template falls as the angle closes, and it is accessible only where both the angle and the bulk driving force allow it.
fig5.caption_key: Colour: f(theta) DG*_hom(Omega_bulk)/k_B T on a logarithmic scale (colour bar), evaluated with the contract functions at the primary state's reference prefactor: the median homogeneous barrier at the median Omega_bulk, scaled to every Omega_bulk at fixed nucleus-liquid energy, molar volume and temperature (the caption states this reference). The vertical axis is the bulk saturation ratio; the template never changes it. Vertical black line: the C3a edge f(theta) = f at cos(theta) = m_cos (configs/preprint/thresholds.yaml). Curved black line: the C3b accessibility bound DG*_het = B_acc at the median B_acc/k_B T. Markers with bars: the screen's median and 5 % to 95 % range of theta and Omega_bulk for each registered state (filled circle, the primary state; open square, each further state in the order of the record). The caption reports the cos(theta) boundary mass of each state (draws clipped to theta = 0 and theta = 180 deg), which is not drawn.

fig6.claim: A few inputs carry most of the variance of the predicted barrier on the template, and those inputs need the tightest precision from first-principles validation.
fig6.caption_key: (a) Variance share of each input in log10 of f(theta) DG*_hom(Omega_bulk)/k_B T (link nucleate, primary state of R-slurry), ranked from the top. With correlated inputs (dependence method gaussian_copula) the share is the Shapley effect (filled circles); with independent inputs it is the Sobol first-order (filled circles) and total-order (open diamonds) index. Bars: confidence intervals at the record's level. (b) Required width of each input's prior relative to its present width, on a logarithmic scale, in the same order (configs/preprint/precision_method.md): bars, status ok; open circle at 1, already clears; cross at the left axis limit, unreachable at any width. The caption names the threshold nearest to each input.

fig7.claim: CaCO3 is thermodynamically stable over a bounded (pH, E) region of the slurry and between two potential limits in the cell; whether each regime's operating range lies inside, and whether a limit is determined at all, decides the stability link.
fig7.caption_key: (a) R-slurry, bulk state (regime activities of Ca2+ and CO3 2-), potential vs SHE. Fill: class of the predominant domain, in the caption's order: CaCO3 solid present; an Al solid without CaCO3; no solid. Thin black lines: boundaries between domains (the caption lists each domain's components by position). Dashed rectangle: the regime's design range of pH and potential (parameter table). The enriched state is not drawn: at equilibrium C5 is decided at the bulk state, and the caption reports the enriched state only as a labelled non-equilibrium sensitivity. (b) R-cell, potential vs Li+/Li. One group of rows per phase (tick label); top row, black: the window used (the lowest oxidation and highest reduction limit over the gas-reference schemes); rows below: each scheme, in the caption's colour order. Solid segment with end ticks: both limits determined. Dotted continuation to the axis edge from an open circle: the limit on that side is undetermined (status undetermined, never read as a pass; the caption gives the reason). Grey band: the regime's operating range E_min to E_max. The caption states the active sink assumption.
